verdict: The chicken tandoori with naan set wins narrowly: lower calories and higher protein. Briyani is still fine with a smart portion.
why: The tandoori set is an estimated 650 kcal, chicken briyani around 750 kcal. About a 100 kcal difference.
Tandoori has 40 g protein compared to 33 g in briyani, so you stay full longer.
Briyani fat is an estimated 29 g vs 25 g, mostly from rice cooked with oil and ghee.
Briyani rice is easy to load up with extra gravy and side dishes. Tandoori chicken is grilled, so there's less added oil.
when_a: Tandoori with naan suits you when you want a tasty meal at a mamak or Indian restaurant but still want to control calories.
when_b: Briyani is okay for a kenduri or the weekend. Ask for half rice and eat it with acar (pickled vegetables).
tip: For tandoori, choose plain naan (not butter or cheese) and add salad. For briyani, reduce the rice and add vegetable dalca.

faq.q: Can I swap naan for chapati?
faq.a: Yes, chapati is much lower in calories. This is an easy way to save hundreds of kcal in one set.

faq.q: Is chicken briyani once a week okay?
faq.a: Okay. What matters is your average calories for the week. Balance it with lighter, high-protein meals on other days.
